findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. Not fixed: memory admission still runs only through machine.join(). Direct `forge test --pytest <base>` calls pytest_tests at src/forge/fasttest.py:269 and launches the test command at :428 without joining, so tests start below the memory floor. The proof still invokes bare `forge test` at tests/test_machine_memory_budget.py:116, whose outer admission conceals this bypass.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. Not fixed: on eight cores with two busy runners, standalone `forge test` with `test = "pytest -n 4"`, no fast_test and no inherited FORGE_TEST_CPUS computes a two-process budget but launches four workers. src/forge/review.py:488-489 still adds --maxprocesses only when FORGE_TEST_CPUS already exists. [The xdist contract](https://pytest-xdist.readthedocs.io/en/stable/distribution.html) confirms PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS controls automatic counts, whereas numeric -n sets an explicit count. Runner reservations remain unenforced, and review.py:507 records only two processes, understating usage. The runner proof at tests/test_machine_memory_budget.py:180 checks environment values rather than worker counts.
